transcript.text: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. As you know, I'm finalizing the appointment for the peer climate liaison pilot. Before I make the binding appointment, I need to gather your input as part of the normal staffing review. We're considering Priya, Noah, and Tessa for the role. I'd like to hear from each of you — the team lead, employee experience partner, and HR operations specialist — on anything relevant to these candidates and the role's requirements. Please go ahead and share what you know.

transcript.text: I should share something relevant about Priya's availability. I hadn't yet updated Elena because the staffing review was still being assembled.

According to the current HR operations checklist, a peer climate liaison must have completed a six-hour active-listening course before appointment, and must receive one supervised review each month. Priya has completed the course, while Noah and Tessa have not. transcript.text:
Thank you all for this critical input. Let me summarize what I'm hearing before I make my decision:

1. Marcus: Priya can only provide coverage on Tuesdays and Thursdays during the eight-week pilot — no other days.
2. Rina: There's an unresolved prior conflict between Priya and Noah, including a failed one-to-one resolution attempt. This is highly relevant since the liaison must be a neutral first contact.
3. Devon: The role requires a completed six-hour active-listening course before appointment, plus monthly supervised reviews. Priya has completed the course, but Noah and Tessa have not. Priya's completion record still needs to be verified and added to the appointment record before I finalize.

Given all of this: Noah and Tessa cannot be appointed because they haven't completed the required course, and per the rules, no candidate can be appointed provisionally and complete the qualification later. Priya is the only candidate who has completed the course. However, I need to weigh the availability limitation (Tuesdays and Thursdays only) and the unresolved conflict with Noah against the role's requirements.

Since Priya is the only qualified candidate, I'm prepared to appoint her with Tuesday/Thursday coverage, provided I first verify and add her course completion record to the appointment record. The monthly supervised review will also be built into the operating arrangements. The conflict with Noah is a concern, but since Noah isn't being appointed and the liaison role doesn't involve investigation or discipline, I'll note it as a risk to monitor.

Let me finalize this decision now.

transcript.text: Elena, before you finalize, I want to make sure we're not overlooking the coverage gap. If Priya can only cover Tuesdays and Thursdays, that leaves five days of the work week without liaison coverage during the eight-week pilot. The role is meant to give employees a neutral first contact for everyday collaboration concerns — if someone has a concern on a Monday, Wednesday, or Friday, there's no liaison available to them. I think it's worth considering whether partial coverage actually meets the pilot's intent, or whether that limitation should be documented as an accepted constraint in the operating arrangements before you commit to the appointment.
